steps.prompt: You have 75 minutes for 25 questions. Is it better to answer all 25, or to leave some blank? Make a guess before the lesson.

cards.title: The test at a glance
cards.body: The AMC 10 has $25$ multiple-choice questions, each with five choices (A) to (E). You get $75$ minutes and no calculator. The questions get harder as you go: about $1$–$10$ are easier, $11$–$20$ medium and $21$–$25$ hard.

cards.title: How scoring works
cards.body: A right answer earns $6$ points, a blank earns $1.5$ and a wrong answer earns $0$. The top score is $25 \times 6 = 150$. Leaving everything blank still gives $25 \times 1.5 = 37.5$.

cards.title: Worked example: a score
cards.text: Leo answers $18$ right, leaves $4$ blank and gets $3$ wrong. His score is $18 \times 6 + 4 \times 1.5 + 3 \times 0 = 108 + 6 = 114$.
cards.note: Wrong answers don't take points away, but they earn less than a blank would have.

cards.title: The common trap: blind guessing
cards.body: A blind guess is right $1$ time in $5$, so on average it is worth $\frac{6}{5} = 1.2$ points: less than a blank's $1.5$. But if you can rule out even two choices, the guess is worth $\frac{6}{3} = 2$ points. Rule out first, then decide.

prompts: When will you leave a question blank, and when will you guess?
How will you pace yourself through the 75 minutes?
